subject: Output baseline current
method: With the migration complete, exercise each circuit in turn and read pmu.oN.current live in the client. Enter the steady figure in pins.baseline_a. Lamps: warm, after two seconds, not the inrush. Motors: mid-travel, not at stall.
expect: One figure per output. More than about 20 percent under est_a is a tired part rather than a bad reading, and that gap is the replacement list (D-025). More than est_a is a fault to find before the soft fuse is set.
note: O21 (0.2 A) and O22 (0.2 A) sit on the 7 A channel's own measurement floor - expect zero, record zero, and give them no band.

subject: Whole-car sleeping current
method: Clamp meter on the battery negative cable - or a meter in series at the disconnect - engine off, doors shut, one hour after key-off so every timer has expired.
expect: 50 mA or under. Above that the extra is the head unit's constant through K11 / F1, the standalone amplifier, the always-hot courtesy lamps on F19, or the pack's own BMS - the PMU's share is the separate bench figure, R6 (D-280).
note: The arithmetic on a 40 Ah pack: about 11 days at 150 mA, about 80 days at 20 mA (D-280). The Ionic IC-12V40-S9H's discharge cut-off is 8.0 V. This reading is what A4's monthly app check is really watching.

when: first start on the new backbone (E12)
subject: Alternator regulated voltage against the pack's ceiling
method: At the battery posts, engine warm, 2000 rpm: headlights off, then headlights and blower on.
expect: 14.6 V or under. The Ionic IC-12V40-S9H states a maximum charge voltage of 14.6 +/- 0.1 V and a float of 13.9 +/- 0.1 V. Above about 14.7 V the fix is the alternator's regulator, never the battery.
note: Lithium starter packs are the reason this reading matters at all - a flooded battery tolerates a high set point and a LiFePO4 pack's BMS answers it by disconnecting. Low-temperature charging is the pack's own problem: its heater handles it, and per the vendor class it draws only from a charging source, so it is not on the sleeping budget (confirm with Ionic - W-330b).

subject: Where water goes when the cowl drains block
method: Dash out. Look at the cowl seam, both windscreen lower corners, the heater case drain and the path each takes to the footwell. Photograph both sides.
expect: A sentence and a photograph per side. Anything whose path would reach the dash node, the PMU or a receptacle moves the bracket or gains a drip loop before the dash node (install section 3 of the v2 plan, archived — 99-ARCHIVE) is cut.
note: This is a look, not a measurement, and it is free while the dash is out. It is the only chance.

subject: Sensor ground offset, engine block to dash
method: Meter between the engine block and the dash GND bus: engine idling, then at full alternator load with headlights, blower and defog on.
expect: Under 50 mV. Above it, the swap's rebuilt engine leg gets a dedicated sensor return - which costs nothing to decide now and a leg to retrofit later.
note: The water-temp and oil senders return through the block; the ICU and the PMU read them against the dash ground, so the offset lands straight on the temperature curve as a few degrees.

subject: The Delayed turn off panel's range
method: In the PMU client: F9, then Delayed turn off. Read the range the Turn off maximum time field accepts, and whether Turn off channel can take an expression.
expect: If maximum time reaches 30 minutes, the KEEP_ALIVE self-hold expression moves into the panel and rules sleep is simplified to match. If it does not, the expression stays exactly as written.
note: No wire changes either way. O22's diode into the wake strip and its drive to K11 stay regardless - the panel replaces an expression, not a conductor.

subject: Stuck-on output
method: For each of O2, O3, O5, O7 and O12 in turn: command the output off in the client and read pmu.oN.voltage.
expect: Zero. Battery volts with .active = 0 is a shorted high-side switch. The PMU has no status for it - OFF / ACTIVE / UNDERCURRENT / OVERCURRENT / THERMAL SHUTDOWN is the entire list - so the detection is a function written against o.voltage and o.active, and it annunciates only.
feeds: work G3; recovery RC01; rules health-band
note: A relay fails open and a high-side FET fails short, so the failure mode changed when the fuse box did. The only certain kill is the master disconnect, which is why RC01 is RC01.

subject: Pop-up motor - the FOURTH conductor
method: On each motor, at the E-03 / E-04 connector: first ohm every pair and every terminal to case at parked, half-raised and raised (WR-case, R-case, RY-case, YG-case, WR-R, WR-RY, R-RY). Then POWERED, on the bench or in the car with a fused lead: WR to +12 V and case to ground; put 12 V on R alone, then RY alone, and note which way the lamp moves and whether it stops on its own; with the motor running, read the voltage on YG.
expect: SP-584 (the 1982 diagram): R (UP) and RY (DOWN) each run through a diode to a cam limit switch driving an internal relay; WR is the motor feed; YG is +12 V while the motor runs (the indicator feed), not a contact to ground. The design caps WR, bridges R and RY, and reads YG on A4 / A5 - if the motor matches the diagram, all three are wrong (block 01.16).
feeds: V-081; D-186; D-199; cavities L2-P 3 / L2-P 4; devices DV11
note: Five minutes more than the check already planned, on the one measurement the pin plan waits on, before the L2 leg is pinned. Do not conclude anything about this motor from the diagram - the diagram is why the extra terminal is being measured (R11).

subject: Wiper motor - which terminal is the park contact's output
method: At the D-02 four-way and the single B terminal: ohm L-case, LB-case, L-LB, L-LW, L-LR and B-case with the arm parked and again mid-sweep. Then power it: 12 V on LW with L to ground, and note whether it runs.
expect: 00-CAR PT678: L is the common brush and the park contact (the +12 V feed in the factory circuit), LB is joined to B away from park and to L at park, and B is the park switch ground on the case. The design feeds LW / LR and reads L as the park output through 12 kOhm into A3, which leaves the armature no return. The redesign (R13) waits on this.
feeds: devices DV15; cavities L2-S 3 and L2-S 4; rules wiper-park; D-317
note: D-317 already reserved L2-S 4 as a park return for a future motor family, so the leg can absorb either answer - but only if this is ohmed before the branch is crimped. Found by T-017, 2026-09-12.

subject: Does the ignition switch's IG contact hold through START?
method: At the ignition switch, meter on the IG terminal, key through OFF - ACC - RUN - START. Watch IG while the key is held at START.
expect: IG stays live at START. The factory circuit implies it - the coils are on IG and the engine fires while cranking - but that is an inference from a diagram and this is a switch in a 44-year-old car (R11). If IG DROPS at START, K13's coil opens mid-crank and the pump stops while cranking: the fix is one more conductor from the switch's ST terminal, diode-OR'd into the coil with a 1N5819 from P071.
note: Five minutes with the cluster out, and it decides whether K13 costs one conductor or two. Take it before the L3 leg is crimped.

subject: Prove the limp-home procedure once
method: In daylight, on the drive: unplug the PMU's 39-way, run recovery RC07 for real - the three fused jumpers from the kit P139, the lever in P - and confirm the car starts, runs and drives. Then restore everything and re-check RC10.
expect: It works, or the procedure is wrong and now is when you find out. Time it: if it takes more than about twenty minutes at a warm bench it will not happen at the roadside in the rain.
feeds: recovery RC01-RC10; D-322; D-353; parts P138 / P139
note: Proving the procedure once is worth more than any part block 00.16 considered. This is the whole reason the kit is carried.

subject: The door and A8 wake stages with the 47 kΩ baselines fitted
method: Bench the two wake stages with the baselines in place and a PMU on the bench. First, three facts the stage values depend on and no document gives (R11): (i) with the PMU unpowered, the resistance from pin 18 (A6) and pin 19 (A8) to ground - the internal pull-up hangs on a dead 5 V rail and may load the line; (ii) the lowest voltage on pin 7 that switches the PMU on, and the current pin 7 draws at 12 V; (iii) the time from pin 7 going high to O22 coming on. Then meter the A6 and A8 line voltage at rest, with each door switch closed and each A8 switch pressed, asleep and awake, and watch wake-strip inputs 3 and 4
expect: At rest: no wake, PMU sleeps (D-248's 30 s, LD17's 30 mA). Any door or A8 switch: wakes. Every state distinct on the ladder
note: Items (i)-(iii) added 2026-09-21 by A10: the v2 stage failed on (ii), and a pulse stage (block 00.26 option b) is sized from (iii) Values are the wake_stages table (D-381). (iii) sizes WS17 / WS27: the pulse ≈ C × ~420 kΩ must outlast the boot with margin - 1 µF ≈ 0.4 s, 2.2 µF ≈ 0.9 s. Also read cold: the rest state must hold Q2 on at 12.0 V (base ~0.71 V)

subject: The CAN message-object timeout's resolution
method: In the PMU client, open a CAN message object (MOB) and enter 0.25 s, then 0.5 s, in its Timeout field. Note what it accepts and what it rounds to
expect: Fractions of a second accepted - the map's timeouts are 250 and 500 ms (can_messages)
note: If only whole seconds: every PMU CAN input times out at 1 s minimum, and the can_messages timeouts for frames the PMU receives are re-derived

subject: A4 and A16 through a real crank
method: In the PMU client, log at the fastest rate it offers: A4 raw, A16 raw, the PMU's supply voltage, and the decoded A4 and A16 states. Meter (min/max hold) between the engine block and the dash GND bus. Car in P, headlamps off: crank until it starts. Then once more with the headlamps switched on just before the key goes to START, so a pop-up is in transit while it cranks. Note the air temperature.
expect: A16 decodes START for the whole crank and O21 never drops out; A4 decodes CRANK_OK (or TRANSIT+PN) throughout. Record the lowest supply voltage and the highest block offset. Block offset over 0.74 V, or A4 leaving P/N on the second crank, means the reserve in D-408: the inhibitor's BW return moves to the dash GND bus (one L1 conductor - a block, it moves a wire). If A16 is decoded on fixed windows (CK15 said no division), a supply under 10.4 V during the crank means the windows are wrong.
feeds: rules ladder-decode; rules crank; inputs A4 / A16; D-408
note: The budget in D-408 assumes up to 0.5 V of block offset (E12's acceptance) and an unmeasured sag on a LiFePO4 pack. E26 calibrates with every output off and CK05 reads only with the engine running, so no other step sees a crank.

subject: Can a PMU function divide, and read the supply voltage?
method: In the PMU client, build a function (or math channel) of the form (a × A16 − b) / (supply voltage − A16) and see whether it is accepted, and whether it compares against fractions such as 0.055. Then see whether a 2-D table can take A16 and the supply voltage as its two axes.
expect: Division accepted: A15 and A16 decode on conductance as rules ladder-decode says. No division but 2-D tables: the table fallback. Neither: fixed windows sized over 11.5-14.8 V, and CK14's lowest cranking voltage decides whether they hold.
feeds: rules ladder-decode; inputs A15 / A16; D-408
note: No wire changes either way - only how the same readings are decoded.

subject: A4 and A5 through a pop-up cycle, and the front-star offset
method: After MG16, with both pop-ups migrated. In the PMU client, log A4 raw, A5 raw, O1 current and the decoded states at the fastest rate. Meter (min/max hold) between the front star stud and the dash GND bus. Engine idling. Switch the headlamps on, then off, three times; then hold a wink.
expect: Each cycle reads IDLE → TRANSIT → IDLE on the moving side and never lands on a fault; A5 with the lever in R reads TRANSIT+R → REVERSE. Front-star offset under 0.28 V while the motors run. Above 0.28 V, TRANSIT+PN can read as TRANSIT: a crank during a pop-up movement would be refused for that second (safe, but note it); above 1.0 V TRANSIT itself leaves its window, and the front star's ground path is the fault to find.
feeds: rules ladder-decode; rules pop-up-cycle; inputs A4 / A5; G05; G07; D-408
note: The transit contact and the 47 kΩ baselines return to the front star (G13), which also carries the motors' current - so the offset is largest exactly when the transit bit is being read. Hand estimate 0.1-0.3 V; nobody has measured it (R11).

subject: Light switch E-01 - its full contact table, with and without flash-to-pass
method: At the switch connector, ohm every terminal pair in OFF, PARK, HEAD LOW and HEAD HIGH, each with the stalk pulled to PASS and released.
expect: SP-473 (1980 manual) shows passing closing the same output as HIGH (E-H), not a contact of its own. The A15 ladder assumes a separate PASS contact (D-184); if SP-473 holds for 1982, a daytime flash decodes as HEAD_LO and raises the lamps.
feeds: devices DV19; ladders A15; D-184; R13
note: Review 2026-09-28. Do not change the ladder from the 1980 table - measure (R11).

subject: Turn / hazard switch and wiper switch - contact tables
method: Ohm every terminal pair of the turn switch (LEFT, neutral, RIGHT, hazard ON) and the wiper switch (OFF, INT, LOW, HIGH, washer).
expect: SP-474 / SP-475 (1980) show no OFF contact to ground on either stalk, and hazard ON joining F-G-H. The A1 / A2 ladders assume an OFF contact and no hazard overlap; if the 1980 tables hold, the 47k is a baseline and every window moves.
feeds: ladders A1, A2; devices DV21, DV22; cavities L3-S1 3 / 4; R13

subject: Oil-pressure sender C-09 - ohms at 0 psi and at warm idle
method: Terminal to block with the engine off, then at warm idle.
expect: SP-787 (1985): open circuit at 0 psi, about 197 ohm at the first mark, 141 ohm at 60 psi. Falling resistance means a falling A7 reading as pressure rises.
feeds: inputs A7; logic FUEL_PUMP; block 01.17; R15

subject: Hatch and fuel-door release solenoids - current
method: Through an ammeter at 12 V for half a second each, in the car or on the bench.
expect: Unknown. The factory OPENER fuse is 20 A (SP-218). O10 trips at 13 A and already carries about 10 A (LD15).
feeds: relays K3 / K4; N85; pins O10; block 01.21

subject: Rear defogger grid - resistance and broken lines
method: Ohms across the grid; then with 12 V on, the voltage along each line to find breaks.
expect: LD10 assumes 10-13 A and nothing has been measured (K-020); the grid is peeling (K-026).
feeds: pins O4; devices DV33; issues K-020, K-026

subject: Washer pump - does it run
method: Reservoir filled, 12 V straight to the pump.
expect: K-022: not working, cause not diagnosed. DV16 reuses the pump.

subject: Headlamps - which wire is low beam
method: Lamps up; 12 V on RY alone, then RL alone; note which filament lights each time.
expect: PT035: RY = low, RL = high (S-001). The design had them the other way until R8 swaps them.
feeds: cavities L2-P 1 / 2; devices DV10; icu_channels IC11; R8

subject: Stud threads and PMU terminal variants at the heavy connections
method: Measure the thread of the alternator B stud, starter B and S, both battery clamp studs and the PMU stud; read the terminal part numbers on the spare PMU housings in hand (the 1.5 mm and the 2.8 mm).
expect: Nothing records these sizes, and the lugs and rings are bought by stud (P064, P079, P095).

subject: ICU carrier fit to the parts in hand
method: Calipers on the DT13-06PA / 12PA (pitch 4.445 and 6.35 mm, flange face to pin field 18.675 mm, the three flange holes - the 12-way's centre hole above all), a Teensy on its headers (rows 15.24 mm, underside clearance), the XIAO (castellation rows 15.24 mm, the u.FL overhang), the 4517's header rows, CN8 on the ME817EV; then the C4 envelope against the 110 × 80 mm outline
expect: each within 0.2 mm of the footprint, or the footprint is redrawn and DRC re-run to zero
note: Raised at F9 (2026-10-09); the DT13 footprints are drawn from TE 114-151046 and B016, never measured (R11)

subject: DCU carrier provisional outline against the centre-stack space
method: Measure depth, width and height behind the centre stack (V-102) and lay the 180 × 80 mm provisional outline, its four M3 holes 4 mm in and the three DT13 flanges on one 165 mm edge against it; then calipers on the DT13-06PA / 08PA / 12PA in hand (pitch 4.45 and 6.35 mm, the three flange posts, flange rear face to board edge)
expect: the board plus the enclosure wall and a fit gap inside the space, the three flanges on one face; otherwise the outline is redrawn (J2 to a short edge first) and DRC re-run to zero
note: Raised at Y5 (2026-10-09); the outline is provisional by D-455, nothing measured (R11)

subject: Enclosure fit, printed
method: After F11 has rebuilt each board and re-exported its STEP, re-run each board's enclosure script (make_enclosure.py beside the board) with ENVELOPE set to C4 / V-102 / V-113 (rc 0 = no interference and the envelope fits); print base, plate and lid in ASA; test-fit a bare board, the DT13s screwed to the plate, the lid closed on its cord
expect: every DT13 housing through its cut-out without touching (0.5 mm a side), the flange seal compressed with the flange flat on the plate, the board on all four bosses unstressed, the lid closing at all four screws; a failure fixes the board or the enclosure parameters, never the model
note: Y7 provisional fit check 2026-10-09: 0 interferences on all eight parts against the three board STEPs. Findings for F11: the DT13-06PA model's housing sits 1.54 mm off its pin field on both boards; the ICU's DT13 models put the flange front face on the board edge while the DCU's put it 3.955 mm beyond - one placement is wrong; the ICU board edge touches its plate (0.005 mm), 0.3 mm back would give margin
